statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = min(R, C). Equivalently, r is the minimum number of cell flips needed either to make every row palindromic or to make every column palindromic; the two goals are alternatives and r is the smaller of their two separate minimum costs.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m >= 1. Let n = len(grid[0]). The grid is valid: n >= 1, m*n <= 200000, for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid[i]) = n, and for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is 0 or 1. Define R as the number of pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < floor(n/2) such that grid[i][j] != grid[i][n-1-j]. Define C as the number of pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < floor(m/2) and 0 <= j < n such that grid[i][j] != grid[m-1-i][j].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if either every row is already palindromic or every column is already palindromic. A row i is palindromic when grid[i][j] = grid[i][n-1-j] for every j with 0 <= j < floor(n/2). A column j is palindromic when grid[i][j] = grid[m-1-i][j] for every i with 0 <= i < floor(m/2).
